question: When should a recurring scheduled agent task persist output to shared durable state (merged trunk) vs isolated ephemeral state (fresh scratch branch per run), and what breaks when it defaults to the latter?
summary: Derived from read-set monotonicity that value only compounds at a write path every future invocation defaults to reading; branch-per-session isolation (correct for reviewed code) silently zeroes out accumulation for append-only bookkeeping data with no reviewer. Matches trunk-based development (merge to trunk >=daily) and event-sourcing (durable log vs disposable worker state) conventions exactly. Confirmed empirically: this repo has ~129 prior first-principles spike branches since 2026-05-01, none merged, only 1 PR ever opened (closed unmerged) -- the backlog/log this task assumes never actually accumulates.
